manifest.title: TiDB + Databricks: Operational Store Meets the Lakehouse
manifest.tagline: TiDB serves live features while Databricks trains and scores on the same fresh data.
manifest.pattern: Data platform teams on Databricks asking how an operational database fits next to the lakehouse.

metrics.label: Operational Write Rate
metrics.howMeasured: Rows inserted into TiDB's events table since the last event-loop tick, divided by EVENT_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS / 1000.

metrics.label: Freshness Lag: TiDB -> Delta
metrics.howMeasured: computeFreshnessLagMs(heartbeatWrittenAtMs, observedAtMs): heartbeatWrittenAtMs parsed from the federated MAX(written_at) read; observedAtMs is Date.now() when that read resolves.

metrics.label: Rows Read by Databricks
metrics.howMeasured: The row_count field of the Statement Execution API response for the scoring INSERT ... SELECT statement.

metrics.label: Reverse-ETL Write Rate
metrics.howMeasured: Scored rows in the upsert batch divided by the wall-clock seconds timed() measured for the single TiDB upsert statement.

metrics.label: Serving Read p50
metrics.howMeasured: summarize() of timed() latencies for SELECT ... FROM customer_risk_scores ORDER BY RAND() LIMIT 1, .p50 field, recomputed each event-loop tick.

metrics.label: Serving Read p99
metrics.howMeasured: Same summarize() call as serving-p50, .p99 field.

metrics.label: Event to Servable Feature
metrics.howMeasured: computeFullLoopSeconds(loopStartMs, writeBackAtMs): loopStartMs is the runner's Date.now() at the last event write before the scoring run started; writeBackAtMs is Date.now() right after the scored rows are read back from Databricks.

metrics.label: Ad Hoc TiFlash Query Latency
metrics.howMeasured: timed() around the single TiFlash-hinted aggregate SELECT issued directly against TiDB when the run-analytics control fires.

phases.label: Steady-State Writes
phases.narration: This is just an app writing to TiDB - purchases, refunds, chargebacks, one row at a time, like any OLTP workload.

phases.label: Databricks Reads TiDB Live
phases.narration: Databricks is now querying TiDB directly - no export job, no staging bucket, just a live JDBC read through Unity Catalog.

phases.label: Reverse ETL: Scores Back to TiDB
phases.narration: The scores Databricks just computed are landing back in TiDB, in a table the app already knows how to query.

phases.label: Serving Fresh Scores
phases.narration: The app is reading those scores right now, in single-digit milliseconds, while new events keep landing.

phases.label: Ad Hoc Analytics on Fresh Data
phases.narration: Same fresh data, same cluster, now answered by the columnar engine instead of the row store - no second database.

phases.label: Changing the Rule Live
phases.narration: Swapping the scoring rule is a SQL change on the Databricks side - nothing in TiDB or the app has to redeploy.

checks.label: Databricks Can Read TiDB
checks.description: The first federated SELECT MAX(written_at) against the TiDB foreign catalog returns a row.

checks.label: Scores Land Back in TiDB
checks.description: The reverse-ETL upsert into customer_risk_scores completes without error.

checks.label: Full Loop Closes
checks.description: computeFullLoopSeconds returns a finite, non-negative duration for the run.

checks.label: OLTP Writes Never Pause
checks.description: No tick during the scoring/write-back window recorded zero event writes.

controls.label: Run scoring now
controls.description: Immediately runs the federated-read -> score -> write-back sequence.

controls.label: Change scoring rule
controls.description: Toggles the scoring rule between velocity and amount for the next run.

controls.label: Run ad hoc analytics
controls.description: Runs one TiFlash-hinted aggregate query against TiDB and times it.

environment.notes: Databricks reads this cluster over Lakehouse Federation; local tiup playground is not used because Databricks cannot reach a laptop behind NAT.
